resources.string: When an OTP field is focused, temporarily watch notifications for a verification code, then fill that field only after you confirm. This service does not read the SMS inbox, does not write to the clipboard, and does not autofill without your confirmation.
Notification access: on, but the service is not connected
Accessibility: on, but the service is not connected
Watching: on (waiting for an OTP notification)
Watching: standby (no OTP field detected yet)

OTP Fill reads notifications after you focus an OTP field or start watching manually. Watching does not stop on its own; it stops only when you tap Stop watching or turn the switch off. When a 4–8 digit code arrives, a half-screen prompt asks whether to fill it. The code is written into the field only after you tap Fill. The full code is not left on the clipboard, and the SMS inbox is never read.
Two system permissions are required: • Notification access: while watching, read the code and a short source name from notifications • Accessibility: detect the OTP field, show the confirm prompt, and fill the field after you agree
Notification access is used only while watching, to extract a verification code. The SMS inbox is not read, and the confirm prompt never shows the full SMS or email body.
Accessibility is used only to detect OTP fields, show the confirm prompt, and fill the focused field after you tap Fill.

Focusing an OTP field in a webpage or app, or tapping Start watching, begins watching notifications. Watching does not stop automatically if you leave the page, switch apps, or wait; it stops only when you tap Stop watching or turn the switch off. Incoming codes always ask for confirmation; nothing is filled silently.
This app does not use the network and does not collect analytics. Turn the switch off to stop watching immediately.
This fills the current OTP field only. The code is not copied to the clipboard.
Could not autofill. Please type the code yourself.
Built-in 6-digit one-time codes. Secrets stay encrypted in this app and can be imported or exported.

Accounts and secrets are encrypted on this device only. They are not uploaded and are not linked to another app. You can scan or import otpauth URIs, this app’s backup files, and Google Authenticator export QR codes (a photo or a live scan). Long-press a code to copy the digits currently on screen; the secret is never copied. Camera permission is requested only when you scan.
No authenticator accounts yet. Tap Add to paste an otpauth URI or enter a secret.
Paste an otpauth://totp URI, or enter the issuer, account name, and Base32 secret. The default is 6 digits, SHA1, refreshing every 30 seconds.
“%1$s” will be removed from this app. This cannot be undone.
Could not open the encrypted store
Turn on Accessibility first so the code can be filled into a field
Could not start the fill prompt
The code is filled only after you confirm on the half-screen prompt
Optionally set a password to encrypt the backup file. If you leave it blank, secrets are stored as plain JSON — keep the file safe.

This backup is encrypted. Enter the password you set when exporting.

Point the camera at an otpauth QR code or a Google Authenticator export code. The camera is used only on this screen.

The camera is used only to scan authenticator QR codes, then closed. It can read otpauth URIs or Google Authenticator export codes.

Shows a confirm notification when a code arrives. Only the extracted code and a short source are included, never the full message body.
If the confirm prompt did not appear over the webpage, some systems need a background-popup or notification permission.
